newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala revises down 96-97 coffee crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala revises down 96-97 coffee crop forecast.

text.p: Guatemala's 1996-1997 coffee harvest will end at 3 million 60 kg bags, a seven percent reduction from predictions of 3.2 million bags made in October, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said Thursday.
"According to a mid-January recount, we are seeing a seven percent reduction (of the forecast) in the harvest," Anacafe vice president William Stixrud told Reuters.
Stixrud said strong rains and cold affected the harvest in the northern Guatemala region of Coban, in the north eastern part of the country and in the east bordering El Salvador and Honduras.

"There were strong rains in August and September. The tails of hurricanes provoked 3-4 day rains and that produces a lot of fungi. The most vulnerable areas were the north, northeast and east," he added.
According to Anacafe, the 1996-1997 harvest is expected to be down 14-15 percent from the 1995-1996 harvest that came in around 3.6 million bags, almost all of which was exported.
A recent rise in international coffee prices was not hugely advantageous to Guatemala because most of the year's crop had been pre-sold before the spike, Stixrud said.
"I would say that 70 percent of Guatemala's coffee had been exported or its price already set, before prices rose. Unfortunately, very few growers were able to sell at the higher prices," he said.
